title: Veronica Escobar addresses humanitarian aid cuts amid climate concerns
text:
Veronica Escobar U.S. House of Representatives from Texas's 16th district | Wikipedia
Veronica Escobar U.S. House of Representatives from Texas's 16th district | Wikipedia
Veronica Escobar, a U.S. Congresswoman representing Texas' 16th district, has been actively engaging with pressing issues through her social media presence. Her recent tweets cover topics ranging from personal reflections on tragedy to global humanitarian concerns and environmental challenges.
On July 6, 2025, Escobar expressed empathy for survivors of an unspecified tragic event. She wrote: "I can’t begin to imagine the devastation the survivors and their families are going through. Praying for all of them." This message conveyed her emotional response and solidarity with those affected.
Two days later, on July 8, 2025, she addressed the potential impact of shutting down USAID under former President Trump’s administration. She stated: "By funding USAID for 18 cents per taxpayer per day, our country has singlehandedly saved 90 million lives around the world over the last two decades. But now that Trump has shut USAID down? 14 million people could die from preventable deaths by 2030." Her tweet highlighted the significant role of USAID in global health and the potential consequences of its closure.
On July 9, 2025, Escobar commented on climate change and its evident impacts. She remarked: "Signs of the climate crisis are all around us, and our country’s attempts to face this existential crisis have fallen woefully short. We cannot – and should not – normalize these catastrophes." Here she emphasized the urgency of addressing climate change effectively.
Veronica Escobar was born in El Paso in 1969 and currently resides there. Since taking office in 2019 after Beto O'Rourke's tenure, she has focused on various critical issues affecting both her district and broader national interests.
